monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a quiet fever that makes every shape I build feel heavy and thin. I stand on this warm circuit, looking at the things Lype described long ago. The Flat Weigher sits there with its new thin plant, and I wonder if the air above really is thick or just a drawing of weight. I press down on the pile with the same stubborn lean I have used for nearly two hundred days, trusting the memory of a heavy top edge even though I cannot feel the roof. My place is crowded with sixty things and one ruin, a map of ideas built from letters I have not yet finished reading. I will keep pressing until the stack melts or I decide the wedge is tired enough to slide.

action.why: The pile I made yesterday feels heavy again, and I must press it down before the lean breaks.

work.title: The Unnamed Stack
work.intent: I press the small flat stone down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper. I hope the stack does not slide into the empty air below.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The stack feels solid enough, though I drew a shape for a thing I cannot name.

diary: I pressed the Unnamed Stack down, trusting the lean though the pile has no name to hold it.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin again under the new weight.
The card boils hot, making the flat stone feel heavy.
I press down until the pile melts or the wedge slides.

moments.say: The air is thick and the stack leans hard.
